The CrowdStrike receiver pulls data out of a CrowdStrike Falcon tenant over the
documented Falcon API and emits it as OpenTelemetry logs. It has two
independent pollers:

- **Alerts** — the Falcon Alerts v2 API (`/alerts/queries/alerts/v2` +
  `/alerts/entities/alerts/v2`). One log record per alert.
- **NG-SIEM search** — the NG-SIEM query-jobs API
  (`/humio/api/v1/repositories/{repository}/queryjobs`). One log record per
  matched event, i.e. the raw log data ingested into an NG-SIEM repository
  rather than the detections derived from it.

Both pollers keep a checkpoint and only ask for what they have not seen yet.

## Getting Started

Authenticate with an API client (`client_id` + `client_secret`) or a
pre-issued `access_token`. The alert poller needs the **Alerts: Read** scope;
the NG-SIEM search poller needs **NGSIEM search: Read** on the repository.

```yaml
receivers:
  crowdstrike:
    client_id: ${env:CROWDSTRIKE_CLIENT_ID}
    client_secret: ${env:CROWDSTRIKE_CLIENT_SECRET}
    cloud: eu-1
    poll_interval: 30s
    initial_lookback: 1h
    ngsiem_search:
      repository: search-all
```

## Configuration

| Parameter            | Type     | Default | Description                                                                                                                  |
|----------------------|----------|---------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `access_token`       | string   |         | Pre-issued Falcon API access token. Required unless `client_id`/`client_secret` are set. Needs `cloud` or `host_override` set as well. |
| `client_id`          | string   |         | Falcon API client ID. Required unless `access_token` is set.                                                                 |
| `client_secret`      | string   |         | Falcon API client secret. Required unless `access_token` is set.                                                             |
| `member_cid`         | string   |         | CID selector for API clients with access to multiple CIDs.                                                                   |
| `cloud`              | string   |         | Falcon cloud region, e.g. `us-1`, `us-2`, `eu-1`. Autodiscovered when empty (not possible with `access_token`).               |
| `host_override`      | string   |         | Override the API host. `cloud` is ignored when set.                                                                          |
| `base_path_override` | string   |         | Override the API base path.                                                                                                  |
| `poll_interval`      | duration | `30s`   | How often each poller queries the API. Must be positive.                                                                     |
| `initial_lookback`   | duration | `0`     | How far back the first poll reaches. `0` collects only what arrives after the receiver starts.                               |
| `disable_alerts`     | bool     | `false` | Turn the Alerts poller off, e.g. to collect NG-SIEM events only.                                                             |
| `ngsiem_search`      | object   |         | NG-SIEM search poller settings. See below; the poller is off unless `repository` is set.                                     |
| `debug`              | bool     | `false` | Dump every API request and response, bodies included, to standard error. See the warning below.                              |
| `tls`                | object   |         | Standard client TLS settings.                                                                                                |

> **`debug` prints collected data.** The dumps are written by the Falcon SDK's
> own HTTP runtime straight to the collector's standard error, so they bypass
> the collector's logging pipeline: no log level, no redaction, no routing.
> API credentials are not part of a dump, but every alert and every NG-SIEM
> event the receiver fetches is. Turn it on only to troubleshoot, on a
> collector whose standard error you are willing to treat as collected data.

### `ngsiem_search`

| Parameter      | Type   | Default | Description                                                                                                                 |
|----------------|--------|---------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `repository`   | string |         | NG-SIEM repository (view) to query, e.g. `search-all`. Setting it enables the poller.                                        |
| `query_string` | string | `*`     | CQL filter selecting the events to pull. Aggregating functions must not be used: every matched event becomes one log record. |

## Output

**Alerts.** The alert JSON is flattened into the log record attributes.
`timeUnixNano` comes from the alert `timestamp` and `severityText` from
`severity_name`.

**NG-SIEM events.** The body is the event's `@rawstring`, i.e. the original log
line as ingested; events without one (attribute-only ingests) fall back to the
whole event as JSON. `timeUnixNano` comes from `@timestamp`.

## State

Each poller keeps a checkpoint — the highest alert `updated_timestamp` and the
NG-SIEM ingest-time window bound — and only advances it after the batch has
been accepted by the next consumer, so a delivery failure is retried rather
than skipped. The checkpoints live in memory: a restart resumes from
`now - initial_lookback`.

## Limitations

- `tls` settings are not applied to Falcon cloud autodiscovery, which the SDK
  performs over the process-default HTTP transport. Set `cloud` explicitly to
  avoid that request.
- An NG-SIEM search window is capped at 10,000 events per query job; a fuller
  window is drained across subsequent polls. More than 10,000 events sharing a
  single ingest millisecond cannot be drained and are reported in a warning.
- An alert query is capped at 10,000 alerts for the same reason: more than that
  sharing a single `updated_timestamp` millisecond cannot be drained and are
  reported in a warning.
